summary: For RPM installs, put `admin_password`, `pg_password`, `automationgateway_admin_password`, `automationgateway_pg_password`, `automationhub_admin_password`, `automationhub_pg_password`, `automationedacontroller_admin_password`, `automationedacontroller_pg_password` (and `registry_password` for connected installs) in the vault, then run `./setup.sh -e @vault.yml --ask-vault-pass`.
questions: How do I pass a vault file to setup.sh?
Which passwords go in the vault for an RPM AAP install?
Is registry_password needed in the vault file?

answer_card.title: RPM install with a vault file
answer_card.answer_md:
`vault.yml` holds:
```yaml
admin_password: <secure_password>
pg_password: <secure_password>
automationgateway_admin_password: <secure_password>
automationgateway_pg_password: <secure_password>
automationhub_admin_password: <secure_password>
automationhub_pg_password: <secure_password>
automationedacontroller_admin_password: <secure_password>
automationedacontroller_pg_password: <secure_password>
registry_password: <secure_cdn_password>  # connected installs
```
Then:
```bash
./setup.sh -e @vault.yml --ask-vault-pass
```
(The guide prints the flag with one dash.)
